Nvidia is **highly exposed to TSMC as a manufacturing supplier**, especially for its leading-edge AI and GPU chips. Nvidia designs its processors but relies on outside foundries to fabricate them; TSMC is its principal advanced-chip manufacturer.

That creates meaningful **supply and geopolitical concentration risk**: a disruption at TSMC—whether from a natural disaster, capacity constraints, or tensions around Taiwan—could limit Nvidia’s ability to ship its most important products. Moving production elsewhere would likely take time and could involve engineering, capacity, and performance trade-offs.

The exposure isn’t necessarily exclusive: Nvidia can use other suppliers for some products or stages of production, and it can hold inventory or secure capacity in advance. But those measures don’t quickly replace TSMC’s role in manufacturing its most advanced chips. I can’t verify Nvidia’s latest supplier mix or the precise share of its production tied to TSMC here.
